text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Tuesday.

LONDON - A firm early showing on Wall Street helped pull British stocks off their earlier lows by the close of business, after a jittery day dogged by worries over rising British interest rates and next month's budget. The FTSE 100 index closed 5.0 points lower at 4,557.8, its fifth straight decline and its lowest close in four weeks.

FRANKFURT - German stocks ended market trade higher and near the session's peak, buoyed by the firmer dollar and German bond market gains. Statements from German Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer that they were on the way to a pact on revaluing Germany's gold reserves gives market modest boost but lack of fresh corporate news kept dealings relatively quiet and range-bound. The 30-share DAX ended market trade up 20.12 points at 3,625.74. In post-close trade, the DAX index stood at 3,655.59.

PARIS - French stocks finished higher for the third consecutive session as investors took heart from some encouraging remarks by the new Socialist leaders and a drop in U.S. leading economic indicators. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 23.04 points, or 0.89 percent, at 2,624.49.

ZURICH - Swiss stocks surged 1 percent to end above 5,200 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) for the first time. The dollar's rise, a favourable interest rate outlook and firming German stocks led stocks higher, Derivative-linked activity and technical factors also sparked buying. The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended up 32.54 points, or 1.0 percent, at 3,291.37.

TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market's benchmark closed at a new high for calendar year, ending above the 20,500 threshold for the first time since December. Strength in stock futures and continued interest in high-technology issues, especially laggards, boosted the index. The 225-share Nikkei average finished the session at 20,563.16, up 111.31 points, or 0.54 percent. It was the highest close since 20,568.38 on Dec. 11.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed sharply lower after setting a new intraday high in the morning, driven down by worries about the outlook for the property market and disappointment in the government land auction. The Hang Seng Index closed down 230.73 points, or 1.54 percent lower, at 14,760.17.

SYDNEY - Profit-taking and a fall on Wall Street saw Australian stocks pull back, giving up most of Monday's gains, but the market remained near its highs. The All Ordinaries Index ended down 12.1 points at 2,613.6.

JOHANNESBURG - A massive 7.4 billion-rand jump in South African May gold and foreign reserves data underlined a strong stock market, although stocks tipped off their peaks toward the close on profit taking, futures-related appetite for shares also aided blue chips' gains with heavyweight financial stocks a favourite, propelling the Johannesburg Stock Exchange's financial index to a new closing high.
The Industrial index finished up 46.4 points at 8,336.8, the All-Share index was up 50.7 to 7,112.0 and the Gold index dipped 8.4 to 1,158.2.
